page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz with a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core processing is a primary bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register poor to weak results. Conversely, multi-threaded execution leverages the 16 dedicated cores effectively, achieving average tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier, though the Passmark memory score is weak, indicating potential latency or throughput limitations under specific memory-intensive workloads.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extreme single-thread compute velocity. Factual performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving falls consistently within the average tier, making it suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and moderate web serving. It also supports light machine learning tasks, demonstrating average text generation speeds for small 135M and medium 7B LLM models, though prompt processing for larger models is weak. The dedicated CPU allocation offers predictable multi-core execution, providing a stable resource profile for enterprise applications requiring high memory density without the premium cost of high-frequency compute hardware.
